# Background
### In this project I was tasked with reproducing a figure taken from the research paper "Effects of hurricane disturbance on stream water concentrations and fluxes in eight tropical forest watersheds of the Luquillo Experimental Forest, Puerto Rico". The figure represents 9 week moving average concentrations of potassium, nitrate-N, magnesium, calcium, and ammonium-N for four different streams in Puerto Rico (PRM, BQ1, BQ2, and BQ3). 
![The figure to reproduce from Schaefer et al. (2000)](ActualFigure.png)

# Data 
### The data was provided via the McDowell and International Institute of Tropical Forestry, and the USDA Forest Service and made available through the Environmental Data Initiative Data Portal. 
### I used the following datasets in my analysis:
- QuebradaCuenca1-Bisley.csv
- QuebradaCuenca2-Bisley.csv
- QuebradaCuenca3-Bisley.csv
- RioMameyesPuenteRoto.csv

# Methods
### Step 1: Read the necessary data in.
### Step 2: Calculated the 9-week moving average for each nutrient at each site and combined that into one dataframe which was then pivoted. 
### Step 3: Tweaked certain settings for the graph including ordering, renaming, and stacking. 

# Results
## 
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
intermediate_output <- read_csv("../output/intermediate_output.csv")
intermediate_output |>
  mutate(
    Nutrients = fct_relevel(
      Nutrients,
      "k_mgl",
      "no3n_ugl",
      "mg_mgl",
      "ca_mgl",
      "nh4n_ugl"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Nutrients = fct_recode(
      Nutrients,
      "K mgl" = "k_mgl",
      "NO3-N ugl" = "no3n_ugl",
      "Mg mgl" = "mg_mgl",
      "Ca mgl" = "ca_mgl",
      "NH4-N ugl" = "nh4n_ugl"
    )
  ) |>
  ## graph
  ggplot(
    mapping = aes(
      x = window_start,
      y = Concentration,
      linetype = stream
    )
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap("Nutrients", scales = "free", ncol = 1, strip.position = "left") +
  labs(
    title = "Concentrations in Bisley, Puerto Rico streams before and after Hurricane Hugo.",
    x = "Years"
  )
```
